findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O failure (file not found, permission denied, truncated file).
findings.failure_mode: Untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle.
findings.fix: Change return type to Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> (or a domain error enum) and use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(...).

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric or out-of-range CSV field.
findings.failure_mode: A single malformed CSV line aborts the entire session load, losing all previously parsed records.
findings.fix: Use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|e| ...)? or match to return a typed parse error. Propagate via Result return type.

findings.problem: as u16 cast on the result of parse::<u32>() silently truncates values > 65535.
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 value like 70000 becomes 4448 with no warning, silently corrupting domain data.
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parts[1].parse::<u32>()?) or parse directly into u16 via .parse::<u16>().map_err(...). Return the error to the caller.

findings.problem: parts[0] accesses Vec by index with no bounds check. If the line has zero bytes before a comma, parts could be empty.
findings.failure_mode: IndexOutOfBounds panic on an empty or whitespace-only CSV line.
findings.fix: Use .first().copied() or .get(0) and handle None with a typed error or skip.

findings.problem: parts[1] accesses Vec by index with no bounds check. A line with only one field (no comma) produces parts with length 1.
findings.failure_mode: IndexOutOfBounds panic on any CSV line missing the second column.
findings.fix: Use .get(1) and handle None with a typed error (e.g., 'expected 2 columns').

findings.problem: Uses split(',').map(...).collect() to extract two fields. Over-allocates into a Vec<String> for a two-field line. split_once handles first-delimiter extraction without collecting all parts.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation per line. On lines with extra commas, collect includes all split parts, silently ignoring extra columns instead of rejecting them.
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').ok_or(Error::BadLine)? to extract exactly two parts, then trim and parse each.

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a hidden side effect inside a data-loading map closure. The functional core (parsing logic) must not perform I/O.
findings.failure_mode: Side effects leak into the parsing pipeline, making the function non-deterministic, harder to test, and producing stdout noise in tests or production.
findings.fix: Remove println! entirely. If logging is needed, make it explicit at the shell boundary (e.g., log the records after loading, or accept a logger callback).

findings.problem: The function load_sessions mixes file I/O (fs::read_to_string), console I/O (println!), and data parsing in a single pipeline with no explicit boundary between shell and core.
findings.failure_mode: Cannot unit-test the parsing logic without mocking the filesystem and capturing stdout. Violates functional-core/imperative-shell separation.
findings.fix: Split into a pure parse_record(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> function and a shell function load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, Error> that calls fs::read_to_string, iterates lines, and delegates to parse_record.

findings.problem: pub struct Record with all pub fields exposes internal representation. No validation at construction time.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can create Record { name: String::new(), value: 0 } or any invalid combination, violating invariants.
findings.fix: Make fields private and provide a constructor or derive builder. Add domain validation if name must be non-empty or value must be in range.

findings.problem: Return type Vec<Record> gives no way to report errors. All fallible operations (file read, parse, index access) are hidden behind unwrap().
findings.failure_mode: No error taxonomy exists for callers to distinguish I/O errors, parse errors, or malformed input.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> where LoadError is an enum with I/O, Parse, and Malformed variants.

no profiler evidence for allocation profile per line in load_sessions
no allocation analysis for Vec<String> per-line allocation in split().collect() path
no command evidence (no cargo fmt check, cargo check, cargo clippy run)
no benchmark/profiler for whether the function is a hot path requiring optimization
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. All production unwrap(), as casts, unchecked indexing, and hidden I/O side effects identified as BLOCKER findings requiring repair before delivery. The entire function is a single monolithic pipeline with no functional-core/imperative-shell separation, no typed errors, no bounds checking, and no performance evidence.
